remember_me.description: A flag indicating whether the user's session should be remembered across browser restarts.

login_attempts.description: The number of consecutive failed login attempts. After a certain threshold, additional verification may be required.

message.content:
I don’t have real‑time access to weather data, so I can’t give you the current conditions in London right now. However, here’s what you can do:

| Option | How to get it |
|--------|---------------|
| **Weather websites** | Visit sites like [BBC Weather](https://www.bbc.co.uk/weather/2643743), [Weather.com](https://weather.com/weather/today/l/London), or [AccuWeather](https://www.accuweather.com/en/gb/london/uk) for up‑to‑date forecasts. |
| **Weather apps** | Use the built‑in weather app on iOS/Android, or download a third‑party app such as Weather Underground, Dark Sky (now integrated into Apple Weather), or the Weather Channel app. |
| **Voice assistants** | Ask Siri, Google Assistant, Alexa, or Cortana: “What’s the weather in London?” |
| **APIs** | If you’re building an app, you can pull data from services like OpenWeatherMap, WeatherAPI, or the Met Office’s public API. |

If you’d like a quick snapshot of what London’s weather typically looks like in a particular month, let me know and I can give you a summary!
message.reasoning: User asks: "what's the weather in london". We need to provide weather info. We don't have real-time data. We can respond that we can't fetch live data. But we can suggest using a weather API or provide typical weather. We can also ask for clarification. Probably best to say we can't fetch live data but can provide typical weather patterns.
